call_query_api.title: Call a query-protocol AWS service
call_query_api.description: Call a service that uses the AWS query protocol -- IAM, STS, SQS, EC2, SNS, RDS, CloudFormation, Auto Scaling and the rest. `action` and `version` name the operation (both come from that service's API reference), and `parameters` carries its arguments. Lists must be pre-flattened into AWS's numbered form, e.g. {"Filters.member.1.Name": "instance-state-name", "Filters.member.1.Value.1": "running"}.

request.description: The whole form body, including `Action` and `Version` -- e.g. {"Action": "DescribeInstances", "Version": "2016-11-15", "MaxResults": "10"}. Both `Action` and `Version` are required by the protocol, and `Version` differs per service.

output.description: The service's response. Query-protocol services answer XML by default, returned here as text unless the service supports JSON.

call_json_api.title: Call a JSON-protocol AWS service
call_json_api.description: Call a service that uses the AWS JSON protocol -- DynamoDB, Athena, Kinesis, KMS, Secrets Manager, CloudWatch Logs, Step Functions, ECS. The operation goes in the `X-Amz-Target` header as `<TargetPrefix>.<Operation>` and the arguments in the JSON body; the target prefix is per service (`DynamoDB_20120810`, `AmazonAthena`, `AWSSecretsManager`) and is documented in that service's API reference.

payload.description: The operation's arguments as JSON, exactly as that service's API reference documents them.

content_type.description: The JSON protocol version the service speaks -- "application/x-amz-json-1.0" (DynamoDB) or "-1.1" (most others).

get_rest_resource.title: Read from a REST-protocol AWS service
get_rest_resource.description: GET a path on a service that exposes a real REST API -- S3, API Gateway, ECR, EventBridge, Inspector, MediaConvert. You supply the path and query exactly as that service's reference documents them.

path.description: The path to call on the configured service, e.g. "/restapis" for API Gateway or "/2015-03-31/functions" for Lambda.

query.description: Query-string parameters as a flat object.

output.description: Whatever the service returns, parsed as JSON where possible.

send_rest_request.title: Write to a REST-protocol AWS service
send_rest_request.description: Send a POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE to a REST-protocol AWS service. The method is yours to choose, so this covers creates, updates and deletes alike -- and can therefore delete real infrastructure, which is why it is flagged destructive.

path.description: The path to call on the configured service.

body.description: The JSON request body, as that service's reference documents it.

query.description: Query-string parameters as a flat object.

method_override.description: For a service that honours it, the verb to apply instead of POST -- "PUT", "PATCH" or "DELETE". Not every AWS service supports the override header; where it does not, use the connector's raw tools.

output.description: Whatever the service returns, parsed as JSON where possible.
